rules.description: Special Leave Petition (Civil) under Article 136 against a civil judgment, decree, determination or order. Cause title or cover says SLP (C), SLP (Civil), or Special Leave Petition (Civil). Not a civil appeal, writ, review, or miscellaneous application.

Special Leave Petition (Criminal) under Article 136 in a criminal proceeding. Cause title or cover says SLP (Crl.), SLP (Criminal), or Special Leave Petition (Criminal). Not a criminal appeal, writ, or review.
Civil Appeal to the Supreme Court of India, including an appeal by High Court certificate or an armed forces tribunal civil appeal. Cause title or cover says Civil Appeal or C.A. Not an SLP (Civil).
Criminal Appeal to the Supreme Court of India. Cause title or cover says Criminal Appeal or Crl.A. Not an SLP (Criminal).
Writ Petition (Civil) under Article 32 of the Constitution for enforcement of fundamental or other civil rights. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Civil) or W.P.(C).
Writ Petition (Criminal) under Article 32 involving personal liberty or a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Writ Petition (Criminal) or W.P.(Crl.).

Transfer Petition (Civil) seeking transfer of a civil case from one High Court or court to another, typically under Article 139A of the Constitution or Section 25 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Civil) or T.P.(C).

Transfer Petition (Criminal) seeking transfer of a criminal case from one court to another, typically under Section 406 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Cause title or cover says Transfer Petition (Criminal) or T.P.(Crl.).
Review Petition (Civil) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court civil judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Civil) or R.P.(C). Not a curative petition.
Review Petition (Criminal) under Article 137 seeking review of a Supreme Court criminal judgment. Cause title or cover says Review Petition (Criminal) or R.P.(Crl.). Not a curative petition.
Original Suit in the Supreme Court under Article 131, typically a dispute between the Union and a State or between States. Cause title or cover says Original Suit or O.S.
Contempt Petition (Civil) for civil contempt of the Supreme Court or of its orders. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Civil) or Cont.P.(C).
Contempt Petition (Criminal) for criminal contempt of the Supreme Court. Cause title or cover says Contempt Petition (Criminal) or Cont.P.(Crl.).
Election Petition in the Supreme Court, including a Presidential or Vice-Presidential election petition. Cause title or cover says Election Petition.

Arbitration Petition in the Supreme Court under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, typically for appointment of an arbitrator or a related arbitration proceeding. Cause title or cover says Arbitration Petition or Arb.P.
Curative Petition (Civil) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a civil matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Civil). Not a review petition.
Curative Petition (Criminal) filed after dismissal of a review petition in a criminal matter. Cause title or cover says Curative Petition (Criminal). Not a review petition.

Miscellaneous Application (M.A.) or Interlocutory Application (I.A.) in a pending Supreme Court matter, including restoration, clarification, modification, listing, or a similar application. Cause title or cover says M.A., I.A., Miscellaneous Application, or Interlocutory Application. Not a fresh SLP, appeal, writ, review, or curative petition.

categories.name: Advocate's Checklist
categories.description: A numbered YES/NO/N.A. advocate checklist (CHECK LIST, CHECKLIST, CHECK-LIST) verifying the petition against Supreme Court filing requirements, ending with the Advocate-on-Record name and signature.

categories.name: Cover Page
categories.description: The outer title sheet of the Supreme Court paper book, usually one page, with IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA at the top, JURISDICTION on the next line, and advocate for the petitioner or respondent at the foot. Often includes For Index Please See Inside.

categories.name: Record of Proceedings
categories.description: This Court's record of proceedings, usually a one-page table of hearing dates and orders, headed RECORD OF PROCEEDING or RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS.

categories.name: AOR's Certificate
categories.description: The Advocate-on-Record certificate after the cause title at the top, headed CERTIFICATE or letter-spaced C E R T I F I C A T E, stating Certified that or CERTIFIED that the Special Leave Petition is confined only to the pleadings before the High Court, Court, or Tribunal whose order is challenged. Ends FILED ON or DRAWN & FILED BY.

categories.name: Index
categories.description: The paper-book index: a table of PARTICULARS OF DOCUMENT and PAGE NO near the front of the filing, headed INDEX. Rows that list Annexure P-n stay Index; they are not the annexure body.

categories.name: Office Report on Limitation
categories.description: The registry office report on limitation (O/R on Limitation), stating whether the petition is within time and any delay in filing or re-filing.

categories.name: Listing Proforma
categories.description: The proforma for first listing (Proforma for First Listing), a table of case particulars including Central Act and The case pertains to. Also headed PROFORMA FOR FIRST LISTING, LISTING PROFORMA, LISTED PROFORMA, or PERFORMA.

categories.name: Synopsis
categories.description: A narrative SYNOPSIS of the case, usually immediately before the list of dates and events.

categories.name: List of Dates & Events
categories.description: A chronological LIST OF DATES or LIST OF DATES & EVENTS, with a date (DD/MM/YYYY or MM/YYYY) before each event.

categories.name: Main Petition
categories.description: This Court's main petition body (Form 28): a Special Leave Petition, transfer petition, or writ or arbitration petition in numbered paragraphs with Grounds, questions of law, and Prayer, ending Drawn By, Filed on, and the advocate for the petitioner. A High Court writ or petition filed as an exhibit is Annexure P-n, not Main Petition.

categories.name: Affidavit
categories.description: A sworn affidavit whose page is headed AFFIDAVIT or letter-spaced A F F I D A V I T, with a Deponent, Verification, and usually a notary stamp. Do not use when the word affidavit appears only as a checklist item or document list inside an Annexure exhibit.

splitting_strategy.custom_instructions: Near-blank scanned pages, such as blank backs or separator sheets, continue the preceding document instead of starting a new segment. Label every page of the PDF; do not leave later exhibit pages uncategorized. Typical Supreme Court paper-book order: Advocate's Checklist, Cover Page, Record of Proceedings, Index, Office Report on Limitation, Listing Proforma, Synopsis, List of Dates & Events, Impugned Order, Main Petition, AOR's Certificate, Affidavit, then Annexure P-1 through Annexure P-n, Appendix, Application 1, Memo of Parties, Memo of Appearance, Vakalatnama, Filing Memo. A page printed OFFICE REPORT ON LIMITATION is Office Report on Limitation, never Cover Page, even if the Supreme Court caption appears at the top. A page with the cause title at the top then CERTIFICATE or C E R T I F I C A T E is AOR's Certificate, not Main Petition, Cover Page, or Affidavit. CERTIFICATE is always printed on that page. Cause title without the word CERTIFICATE is Cover Page or Main Petition. Main Petition is Form 28 in this Court; it appears once as contiguous pages and cannot reappear after it ends. Assign Annexure P-1 through Annexure P-15 from the printed mark, including slash forms ANNEXURE-P/2, ANNEXURE P/2, ANNEXURE-P2, ANNEXURE P-2, and ANNEXURE-P-2. Keep every following page in that annexure until the next ANNEXURE-P/m heading, even when OCR is poor or the text looks like a High Court writ. Stop at P-15. Do not invent a number and do not use a generic Annexures category. A High Court petition inside an exhibit stays that Annexure P-n, not Main Petition. An Index or List of Dates that merely lists Annexure P-n is still Index or List of Dates. Affidavit is only the sworn AFFIDAVIT leaf, not checklist lines inside annexures. Assign Application 1 through Application 15 in filing order, one category per APPLICATION headed RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH in this Court. Stop at 15. A page headed Annexure P-n is that annexure, not an Application. INDEX OF FILING, FILING INDEX, or FILING MEMO is Filing Memo, not Index.
